description_full: Inspire Medical Systems, Inc., a medical technology company, focuses on the development and commercialization of minimally invasive solutions for patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) in the United States and internationally. The company offers Inspire system, a neurostimulation technology that provides a safe and effective treatment for patients with moderate to severe OSA. It also develops a novel, closed-loop solution that continuously monitors a patient's breathing and delivers mild hypoglossal nerve stimulation to maintain an open airway. The company was incorporated in 2007 and is headquartered in Golden Valley, Minnesota.

CEO compensation is 3× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags moderate compensation governance risk (4/10).
financial_summary: Inspire Medical Systems, Inc. is a small-cap healthcare business with a $1.9B market cap on $912M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +31% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +8.0pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at -51% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests. Gross margins of 85% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $78M in free cash flow — roughly 9 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 0.80× cash conversion.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 9.4% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and stock-based comp at 14% of revenue is silent dilution an owner has to account for, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.
